articles.title: Iran calls out Trump's ‘lies’ about US control over the Strait of Hormuz
articles.description: A spokesman for Iran's military command on Thursday called out US President Donald Trump's "lies and fabrications" after he claimed on social media that Washington had "total control over the Strait of Hormuz". Iran has maintained control of the Strait, a vital energy conduit, since the outbreak of the war on February 28.

articles.title: Rebuilding Aleppo: Syria's war-torn economic capital enjoys gradual rebirth
articles.description: Syria's economic capital Aleppo was left largely in ruins by the fighting that raged there between regime and rebel forces from 2012 to 2016. A 2023 earthquake also caused severe damage to the old city. But reconstruction is now well underway, in particular of Aleppo's treasured historic monuments.

articles.title: Israel sends troops to settler siege as US ambassador slams 'act of terror'
articles.description: Israeli forces on Thursday moved against rogue settlers laying siege to Palestinians amid unusually strong US criticism, even as Israel inaugurated an emblematic settlement elsewhere in the West Bank.

related.title: US ambassador to Israel slams settler siege against West Bank Palestinians as ‘terror’
related.description: US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee on Thursday denounced a siege by Israeli settlers against Palestinians in the West Bank village of Qusra as a "horrific act of terror". Huckabee, an evangelical Christian pastor who in the past has embraced Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, said the Israeli army intervened on Wednesday after a US request, but the soldiers failed to remove the settlers.

articles.title: Japan summons Russian ambassador after Putin’s visit to disputed Kuril islands

Tokyo maintains its claim to the disputed islands near Japan's northernmost Hokkaido island since they were seized by the Soviet Union in 1945.

Tout cessez-le-feu sera utilisé par la partie ukrainienne pour se regrouper et renforcer ses forces », a insisté le vice-ministre des affaires étrangères russe.

articles.title: Solar eclipse 2026: Africa witnesses partial eclipse
articles.description: Part of the world turned its eyes to the skies this Wednesday. The eclipse was also visible across Africa. In Tabarka, where the phenomenon was most pronounced in Tunisia, 59.06% of the Sun was obscured. The partial eclipse was also visible from Dakar and several regions of Senegal, with a maximum of around 37% of the Sun's disk obscured towards the end of the day. And to make sure they didn't miss the celestial event, our correspondents in Tunisia and Senegal also put on their special eclipse g

articles.title: Russia-Ukraine war: Grain hub attacks raise fears over global food prices
articles.description: Kyiv and Moscow have been trading attacks on each other's grain warehouses, as concerns mount that global food prices could rise as a result. Russia struck Ukraine's largest grain shipment port on the Danube overnight, causing damage and setting off a fire. The attack came a day after Ukraine hit Novorossiysk, a major grain hub in Russia's part of the Black Sea.

articles.title: Colombia rescuers cling to hope as quake survival window closes
articles.description: Rescuers in Colombia made a last-ditch effort to locate earthquake survivors early Thursday, as the critical 72-hour window for finding people alive drew to a close. Our journalist Rosa Perez gives us the lastest information.

articles.title: European drought shrivels crops despite farmers’ best efforts to adapt
articles.description: The drought roasting much of Europe this summer is taking a heavy toll on crops across the continent, from potatoes in the Netherlands to corn in Bosnia. Triodos, a Dutch bank with a focus on sustainability, has warned that this could reduce gross domestic product across the EU by 1 percent for 2026 – or around €180 billion.

articles.title: Eurovision: Winners involved in 'armed conflict' now ineligible to host contest
articles.description: The winning country in Eurovision will be ineligible to host the contest the following year if involved in an armed conflict or a "sensitive geopolitical situation" that could impact the safety of the event, organisers said on August 12. The rules for the contest were updated following an annual review by the European Broadcasting Union.

articles.title: L’Ukraine revendique la destruction du système de protection aérienne du palais de Poutine au bord de la mer noire
articles.description: Des drones ukrainiens ont détruit des systèmes de défense électronique à vingt kilomètres du palais du président russe Vladimir Poutine, le laissant sans défense, selon un commandant de l’armée ukrainienne.

articles.title: Gaza's beekeepers are rebuilding their livelihoods amid the ruins of war
articles.description: Amid the rubble and debris of Gaza's bombed-out landscape, beekeepers are rebuilding their livelihoods, handling swarms and collecting what little honey they can from the colonies that survived the war. Ibrahim al-Dabbeh, head of the Cooperative Association of Beekeepers in the Gaza Strip says "the war destroyed more than 95% of the bee sector". Rebuilding these hives means trying to revive an industry pushed to the brink of extinction.

articles.title: West Bank: "In recent weeks, we've seen a striking escalation in violent acts"
articles.description: Israeli forces on Thursday moved against rogue settlers laying siege to Palestinians amid unusually strong US criticism, even as Israel inaugurated an emblematic settlement elsewhere in the West Bank. Our correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky tells us more.

articles.title: Russian strike on Ukraine passenger train kills 2
articles.description: A Russian drone attack on a train carrying hundreds of passengers in southern Ukraine killed two people on Thursday. Our correspondent Emmanuelle Chaze tells us more.

articles.title: 🔴 Mali pardons French official Yann ​Vézilier, who was sentenced to 20 years in prison
articles.description: Mali President Assimi Goïta on Thursday pardoned a French ​national who had been sentenced to 20 years in prison. Last year, Mali's military-led government accused Yann ​Vézilier, an official from the French embassy, of being involved in a plot ​to destabilise the West ‌African country.

articles.title: West Bank: "What we see is an escalation in methods"
articles.description: Israeli settlers have besieged three homes in the occupied West Bank for several days, including one owned by a Palestinian American, in what the US ambassador called a "horrific act of terror" on Thursday. We discuss the situation with our guest, Allegra Pacheco, chief of party of the West Bank Protection Consortium.

articles.title: Russian detained over plot to 'execute' Ukrainian-American in Warsaw, Tusk says
articles.description: Poland has arrested a Russian national who was allegedly hired to plan an "execution" targeting a Ukrainian-American dual citizen in Warsaw, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Thursday. Tusk said it was the first time that “someone on the order of Russia” had sought to attack an American citizen on NATO territory.

articles.title: Zambia voters weigh Hichilema's economic record
articles.description: Zambians went to the polls Thursday in an election focused on economic hardships in the copper-rich nation, where President Hakainde Hichilema is seeking a second term.

articles.title: L’éditorial de Philippe Gélie : « Xi Jinping, le marionnettiste chinois qui veut doubler l’Amérique en 2049 »
articles.description: En tirant les leçons des guerres en Ukraine et au Moyen-Orient, la Chine utilise ses alliés russe et iranien comme des aiguillons dans sa rivalité avec Washington.

articles.title: "Je pense que nous allons le garder" : Donald Trump revendique un contrôle "total" du détroit d'Ormuz, l'Iran dément
articles.description: "On reste discrets", a déclaré Donald Trump au média en ligne Axios en évoquant la nouvelle stratégie des Etats-Unis en Iran.

articles.title: Jury selection begins in Meta youth harms trial in California federal court
articles.description: Jury selection began Wednesday in Meta's federal trial over claims its platforms have harmed youth mental health and also track children in violation of federal law. Our correspondent Wassim Cornet tells us more.
